decisions.quote: To date, only one small-scale study has been published in this area (Camuffo et al., 2020). It reported that entrepreneurs taught to use a scientific approach to decision-making were more likely to terminate their projects and to pivot radically. But the study's small scale and specific institutional setting create natural boundaries to the credibility and generalizability of these results. A large-scale replication in other settings is therefore critical to establish the validity of this approach.

Row1242names a different 2008BreathingShoes industrycase paper while copying the same pivot/termination results. Replacing1242with2020would duplicate603, not recover another original. Retain603 and remove1242. Full design and supplied complete counterpart set independently checked; this is substantive target evidence, not date/DOI-only exclusion.

decisions.quote: Our research design combines four randomized control trials (RCTs), including Camuffo et al.'s (2020), which was carried out in Milan in 2016. The three additional RCTs apply the same intervention (with minor adaptations due to operational and contextual constraints) across different contexts and time windows (Milan in 2017, Turin in 2018, London in 2019).
decisions.reason: The paper collects new experimental data across three additional randomized control trials (Milan 2017, Turin 2018, and London 2019) to re-test the findings of Camuffo et al. (2020), which makes it a replication under the codebook.
